notes.title: V1.07d-1 Major Patch Released!!
notes.content:
Dear all,

I'm proud to announce that Foresight's major patch V1.07d has been released. This patch in essence will be delivered in a few stages subjected to further fine tuning based on new features and modified gameplay experience.

Therefore, we'll start with V1.07d-1.

The core features implemented in V1.07d are already in the patch. What remains will be the fine tunings and additional contents to be added along the way. This takes time and we have to find a balance between holding off the patch too long or releasing it in stages.

Therefore here it goes:

Implementations
- You can now attack-move using the minimap. Press 'A' / Attack button, click on the minimap, a red ping will appear signifying acknowledgement.
- Textures have been improved, streamlined and sharpened in some cases to better bring out the details.
- The 3 core buttons will now have its UI bracket containing them instead of being "naked".
- Implemented speed button which allows you to adjust the speed of the game between 1.0x (default), 1.5x and 2.0x. It works by cycling between the 3 options.
- Implemented an "immediate" objectives widget which presents the most current and immediate objective to be completed in greater detail. While taking up the space used for entering chat messages; it'll switch between so that there'll be no overlaps.
- Added more details into the Introduction cutscene. Watch it again to see the changes!
- Added key shortcut to zoom in/out using Ctrl + Up/Down. (Up/Down is based on scrolling the map up and down respectively)
- Revamped tutorial mission 1 and 2. (Mission 3 will require more time to revamp and will not feature in this patch, we're sorry about that)
- Implemented new button - Strict Target mode to force a ship to target ship types based on its designation. Anti-fighter ships will only target fighters and nothing else. Holding SHIFT will always set mode to true. Right-clicking on the button will always set mode to false. An indicator appears on top of the ship if the mode is switched on to keep you reminded.
- Implemented target prioritization for ships. Doing an attack move won't cause the ships to attack anything that is RED first. As of V1.07d onwards, all ships (not turrets) will prioritize enemy turrets first, enemy ships second, enemy command centers third, and lastly any others. This is in response to early feedback that the ships shoots at anything that is red. Took us some time to really figure out. P.S. This doesn't work if YOU give your ships a explicit target; it'll still obey your orders.

AI players will have this feature automatically as well. So don't be surprised if they're attacking your turrets more often than anything else.

- Target prioritization for ships under attack is slightly different as well. On top of hierarchy, it'll also check if the last attacker has a higher threat rating by damage and will change to attack the stronger target first. (ie, between a UNC Missile Turret and a UNC Frigate, the ship may attack the frigate instead).

Modifications
- Foresight ships' max speed has been increased by 15% across the board. Acceleration, deceleration and rotating speeds are not affected.
- All Foresight projectiles, lasers, bolts, etc have received an 20% increased overall for all acceleration, deceleration and maximum speed. Again, rotation speeds if any aren't affected.
- Improved Foresight's reliability baseline. Construction and build progress timings are now closely tied to render factor performance instead of pure real-time which may not reflect properly when the game is lags.

Bug Fixes
- Multi-construction feature has a bug when you group a bunch of builders, ie, UNC Outposts into a group, then selecting the group to construct, ie, a UNC Heavy Turret. When you select the whole group again, you may not be able to build anything at all. (ie, click on the structure icon and nothing happens). This is fixed. Structures that are busy won't be considered even if it's selected (due to grouping).
- Fixed a bug when right-clicking on the main bottom panel actually triggers a smart click.
- Fixed a bug where fleet panels flashing red indicating the fleet under attack doesn't return to white.
- Fixed a bug where ships assigned to Pursue and Destroy standing orders moving across wormholes, encountering enemy ships, and destroying them, after which, they'll go into guard mode instead of continuing their journey.
- Fixed a bug where continuation of journey after winning a battle into other sectors causes the ships to turn a BIG ROUND before moving on. This is due to a safety flag that was accidentally passed into the flight path creation. (when the ship has strayed off-course into another sector during the fighting)
- Fixed list box from showing text items that eat into the next line. This is caused by the font sizes being set after the width and height is being anticipated, causing the anticipation to be inaccurate.
- Fixed a bug where the Strategic Map (global map) is open showing all the sectors, you press the options button (instead of ESC) and the map closes, but the options button becomes disabled. Now the button will guarantee direct passage into the options menu regardless.
- Fixed a bug between the accumulators (showing how much hp, how much gas harvester, default view) and the speech view (story telling) where both might appear at the same time overlapping each other.
- Fixed a bug in the final mission where the prime target (no spoilers here) doesn't go to its final destination; instead, either going into guard mode or just hanging there doing nothing, sending the mission into a limbo.

Conclusion

We'll continue to keep implementing new features and fixing bugs regardless of new/old. Some feedback require more time than others for us to come up with a proper solution. While you have every right to be unhappy with us for being slow, please try to understand that we're doing our very best.

Issues and feedbacks are actually tracked in our bug tracking system and are never forgotten.

For the next 1-2 weeks, we'll be hardening V1.07d patch, revise some mission AI to be more aggressive and revamping tutorial mission 3. All these take more time to test and balance than just develop.

After that, we'll finally ... FINALLY go into our multiplayer lobby. Which is V1.08.

Thanks for your patience, feedbacks and support over these months. It kept us going and we look forward to improving your experience even further.

Have a nice week ahead!
Jeremy

notes.title: Request for feedback - Game Speed
notes.content:
Dear all,

This has been going around for quite some time already. It's probably time to address this issue in full.

Folks have complained that the game is slow. I've observed that it's slower when the player is only controlling Lock (ie, tutorials, scout missions, etc) but not as slow when playing a full game or a mission with multiple ships.

We could increase the speed of the game for all the ships AND weapons but that'll definitely make things a little harder - such as ambush, flank attacks, etc.

Therefore, I'll like to request for a feedback - how much increase is good?

Points to take note:
- We're currently looking at the maximum cruising speeds only. Acceleration and deceleration isn't considered.
- Having a faster game means that there's a higher chance the collision detection may miss. The retrospection mechanism is turned off to improve performance.
- Faster ships means faster reaction times, which means fighters and bombers will be invaluable and is a must-have.
- We're looking at a 10-15% increase in maximum cruising speed, and a 10-15% increase in ALL weapon speeds (max speed, acceleration and deceleration).

Please share your views. Thanks!

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: V1.07c-3 patch released!
notes.content:
Dear all,

We're proud to announce that V1.07c-3 patch has been released. There's however, a slight problem with the resolution and you may be required to set your resolution once more due to a more stringent check against the resolution with refresh frequency. This is a slight inconvenience and will not affect new installations.

Build ID: 711209

New Implementations

- A direct objective text implemented to show the next immediate objective. However, this is not in use just yet. We'll revamp the tutorial missions and other missions that require such a device to keep you informed.

- 3 buttons added for the following purposes:
1) Objectives (click to show)
2) Messages (logs, system messages)
3) Options menu button

These buttons will actually animate to inform you that there has been a change or significant updates made to either the objectives or messages that require your attention.

We hope that with these 3 buttons, things will be more accessible than having to go to the shortcuts to map the keys.

- Added a small feature whereby if you press SHIFT and right-click on the fleet panel, all non-essential messages are removed.
- Fleet ID text ie "Fleet 1 (9/25)" now blink RED whenever the fleet is under attack. Removing the need to keep monitoring the fleet panel. This feature however, may not always return the Fleet ID back to white all the time. We'll look into it and get it fixed by the next patch.
- Implemented the Ship Invulnerability Package where ships can be assigned to be indestructible, invulnerable or have limited vulnerability with a minimum HP guard. These are code-governed and therefore will be very reliable. Cheat codes will not break the package's functionalities too.

Modifications
- Enhanced the particle culling system relative to its size and distance from the camera. This means if a particle appears to be so small that it's barely a pixel on screen, it will NOT be rendered. This applies only to non-essential particles. All projectiles will always be rendered regardless of their size.

You can set the sensitivity of distance by tweaking the Particle Density option. A Low setting means that smaller particles tend to disappear nearer towards you while a High setting means otherwise.

We believe that this will improve your overall Foresight experience since we can now handle lesser particles that has little or no impact on your visual experience.

- All camera locks in Mission 1 removed. Now you'll always be free to move the camera around.
- Improved the speed of flow for the main menu - you don't have to wait for a few seconds before things occur. Now they're shortened to as concise as possible.

Bug fixes

- Fixed a perculiar bug that occurs only on 1280x1024 resolution where in the mission briefing, the text will overflow out of the briefing panel.
- Fixed a bug where text within a list box will sometimes get messed up with lines overlapping each other. (this has occured to fleet panels as well)
- Fixed a bug where auto-fleet creation doesn't take leadership stats into consideration. Only rank was considered and it's definitely insufficient especially when you have more than 1 captain onboard. Now rank is considered first, then leadership stats sort is applied and the personnel with the highest rank and leadership will always be chosen.
- Fixed a bug where in some cases, the in-game speech dialogue will actually overflow out of its area.
- Fixed a bug where strange symptoms occurred to particle emitters who were trying to emit but couldn't. This occured to Mission 5 UNC Gunships where their missiles totally had no trail. As well as Mission 23 where the NSAU Mobile Power Unit doesn't emit the distorted shockwave consistently.
- Fixed a bug where upon closing the Strategic Map (showing all the sectors) will always minimize all the fleet panels automatically. Now if you had 
- Fixed a bug where fleet panel messages don't blink as they should ... and that their effect objects are actually leaked due to constant insertion without removal.
- Fixed a bug in Finale mission where the mission critical craft actually gets its invulnerability lifted prematurely ... allowing the player to destroy it too soon causing the mission to go into a limbo.

Conclusion

More bug fixes to come. Tutorial will be revamped next along with a new trailer for Foresight!

P.S. Yes, there ARE cheat codes in Foresight.

Regards,
Jeremy

- A direct objective text implemented to show the next immediate objective. However, this is not in use just yet. We'll revamp the tutorial missions and other missions that require such a device to keep you informed.

- 3 buttons added for the following purposes:
1) Objectives (click to show)
2) Messages (logs, system messages)
3) Options menu button

These buttons will actually animate to inform you that there has been a change or significant updates made to either the objectives or messages that require your attention.

We hope that with these 3 buttons, things will be more accessible than having to go to the shortcuts to map the keys.

- Added a small feature whereby if you press SHIFT and right-click on the fleet panel, all non-essential messages are removed.
- Fleet ID text ie "Fleet 1 (9/25)" now blink RED whenever the fleet is under attack. Removing the need to keep monitoring the fleet panel. This feature however, may not always return the Fleet ID back to white all the time. We'll look into it and get it fixed by the next patch.
- Implemented the Ship Invulnerability Package where ships can be assigned to be indestructible, invulnerable or have limited vulnerability with a minimum HP guard. These are code-governed and therefore will be very reliable. Cheat codes will not break the package's functionalities too.

Modifications
- Enhanced the particle culling system relative to its size and distance from the camera. This means if a particle appears to be so small that it's barely a pixel on screen, it will NOT be rendered. This applies only to non-essential particles. All projectiles will always be rendered regardless of their size.

You can set the sensitivity of distance by tweaking the Particle Density option. A Low setting means that smaller particles tend to disappear nearer towards you while a High setting means otherwise.

We believe that this will improve your overall Foresight experience since we can now handle lesser particles that has little or no impact on your visual experience.

- All camera locks in Mission 1 removed. Now you'll always be free to move the camera around.
- Improved the speed of flow for the main menu - you don't have to wait for a few seconds before things occur. Now they're shortened to as concise as possible.

Bug fixes

- Fixed a perculiar bug that occurs only on 1280x1024 resolution where in the mission briefing, the text will overflow out of the briefing panel.
- Fixed a bug where text within a list box will sometimes get messed up with lines overlapping each other. (this has occured to fleet panels as well)
- Fixed a bug where auto-fleet creation doesn't take leadership stats into consideration. Only rank was considered and it's definitely insufficient especially when you have more than 1 captain onboard. Now rank is considered first, then leadership stats sort is applied and the personnel with the highest rank and leadership will always be chosen.
- Fixed a bug where in some cases, the in-game speech dialogue will actually overflow out of its area.
- Fixed a bug where strange symptoms occurred to particle emitters who were trying to emit but couldn't. This occured to Mission 5 UNC Gunships where their missiles totally had no trail. As well as Mission 23 where the NSAU Mobile Power Unit doesn't emit the distorted shockwave consistently.
- Fixed a bug where upon closing the Strategic Map (showing all the sectors) will always minimize all the fleet panels automatically. Now if you had 
- Fixed a bug where fleet panel messages don't blink as they should ... and that their effect objects are actually leaked due to constant insertion without removal.
- Fixed a bug in Finale mission where the mission critical craft actually gets its invulnerability lifted prematurely ... allowing the player to destroy it too soon causing the mission to go into a limbo.

Conclusion

More bug fixes to come. Tutorial will be revamped next along with a new trailer for Foresight!

P.S. Yes, there ARE cheat codes in Foresight.

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Big Fat Tip #2 - Dead ships and fighter central command
notes.content:
Dear all,

2 tips today!

1) Broken pieces from dead ships

Dead ships - when they break into pieces, can temporarily be a bullet sponge for others to escape enemy fire. While this is true, the broken pieces can also be deflected by indirect fire; you can't target the broken pieces but you can try to shoot through them.

This was done to counter-balance the bullet sponge effect where dead ships have the ability to absorb more damage than its original hit points.

So... how can I deflect the dead ship pieces if I can't target them? Just keep firing at the target behind!

2) Fighter Central AI

This may appear to be very subtle to most players but every player actually has a central command system which keeps track of how many of its own fighters are actually engaging a single enemy fighter.

The system currently allows a maximum of 5 friendly fighters vs 1 enemy fighter.

This means if you have 50 fighters and there's only 2-3 enemy fighters... only 15 of your fighters will engage these 3 enemy fighters at any one time. 

This system was designed for 3 reasons:
1) Performance - if fighter swarms are allowed for enemy fighters, then there'll be a huge number of fire power discharged in the game with little purpose and is totally inefficient.
2) Prevent unrealistic battle experience where you'll see a single enemy fighter being swarmed by a huge number of fighters. That's unrealistic and in reality, chances of fratricide is very very high.
3) It diverts attention away even when precious fighters can be engaging other more high value targets such as enemy bombers. It can be frustrating if ALL the fighters only engage 1 target at a time.

This being said - it doesn't apply to ships and structures. Fighters can by all means swarm an enemy ship or structure. The fighter central command doesn't apply in this scenario.

So - that's the reason why your fighters aren't doing silly things just when you might need them the most attacking other enemy bombers or fighters attacking your capital ships.

Conclusion

There're many such little gems hidden in the game - not on purpose - but they're just harder to observe. Will share more of such information next week!

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Patch V1.07c-2 RELEASED!
notes.content:
Dear all,

V1.07c-2 has been formally released. It has some changes compared to the staging build - so please opt out of the staging build at once.

Implementations

- Due to the negative feedback received on the voice acting, we managed to dig further and discovered that it was a certain character's voice - in this case, Pugalenthi - that was the problem.

Know this - I'm not proud of replacing my team's work and will never do so at a whim unless absolutely necessary.

As a result, we've gotten a new voice actor for Pugalenthi and has since replaced all his lines with some modifications to the dialogue.

- Performance behavior changed. Now, a low frame rate will not prevent particles from being emitted - but it'll prevent them from ever being rendered until the frame rate improves. The only direct housekeeping factor is the absolute particle limit - set to remove all non-essential particles such as burn trails, smoke, explosion debris, etc to improve performance. This removal is done by both during emission (prevention) and particle life (housekeeping).

All essential particles will never be subjected to performance limits.

Fixes

- Adjusted pacing for Pugalenthi's Dismissal Cutscene.
- Mobile Refinery view appears at the scoreboard. This is now fixed.
- Custom paths not properly rendered when player plots a destination into uncharted space. This is largely due to the path finder's inability to create a "safety" path. As such, it's now decided that a direct reckless movement into uncharted space will be regard as a NON-safety path.

There'll still be certain cases where the path finder will fail to create a path. Upon which, you may be required to plot the path to your destination manually.

Please remember that when safety is specified, the path finder DOES take current enemy activities into consideration. This holds true only as long as the sector is monitored by scouts. As intelligence data expire, it'll no longer reflect enemy presence and thus will be regarded as part of a safe route.

So please don't ask me why your ships tend to charge into enemy bases when you didn't monitor them closely with scouts set into dormant mode.

- Fixed a regression with fleet controls behaving weirdly. This is a major regression error in V1.07c-1 and has since been fixed. We're sorry about it. Originated from the error that fleets do NOT report their inability to traverse to destination.
- Fixed a bug with Burn Effect vs Ships w/shields. Now instead of burning the ship itself, it'll burn around the shields so correct depict the effect.
- Fixed a bug in Pugalenthi's Dismissal cutscene where a repeat of it will cause the cutscene to show ONLY 1 scene.
- Fixed a bug where the outer fog is shown after viewing a cutscene.
- Fixed a bug where fleet commanders keep playing the wrong VO - instead, awakening from dormant voice is played instead.
- Fixed a slightly rare scenario where newly deployed fighters from a mothership that has been set to "Silent Tail" standing orders will actually retaliate against the attacker. By definition - no ships or fighters belonging to that ship should retaliate when under "Silent Tail" standing orders.

Known Issues

We have several existing issues that has yet to be fixed. We're not at liberty to reveal them here lest it spoils your fun. We'll be working on them to fix them asap.

Conclusion

We hope that you'll have a 2nd look at Foresight. Take a listen to Pugalenthi's new voice, see what we've changed and/or improved so far. We're listening to you and will always do to make our games better.

Thanks for your support as always!

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Announcing V1.07c-2 patch
notes.content:
Dear all,

Yes. We're finally almost there. V1.07c-2 patch will continue its set of bug fixes and the big thing about it is that Pugalenthi will get his new voice over finally.

All the mission briefing voices will be re-processed - addressing the issues of imbalanced volumes between characters. There's a reason behind this - originally the briefing room is STEREO - that means if Jun Jimin is on the right, her voice will come from the right.

But as feedback came in - different machines perceived this volume differently - as a result some were softer than most. Therefore those voices were adjusted to be 2x louder.

But persistent feedback and recommendations finally got us changing it to just basic voices. This caused the previously re-normalized voices to sound a lot louder than usual.

We're sorry for that and we'll definitely address those issues once and for all in the upcoming patch - which we'll try to deploy by tomorrow.

Thanks again for your support and feedback.
Jeremy

notes.title: Reminder: You can quick save/load!
notes.content:
Dear all,

In case you missed it, Foresight DOES have a quick save and quick load functionality. This is to save you folks the unnecessary navigation through the clunky options menu.

In fact, it's made to help you save without the need of ever going into the options menu.

How to start quick save/load?

You need to save at least ONCE. Press F6 to start the proceedings. The game will prompt that you need to save at least once.

Select your save slot - that will be your default quick save slot for your current game. Do not overwrite this slot or else quick save will overwrite it the next time you quick save.

Subsequently, you'll just need to press F6 to quick save. A prompt will appear to confirm. 

Press YES to save. 

There'll be a notification that tells you "Game saved." as a notification.

How to quick load?

You must have quick-saved at least once, establishing the slot. Press F7 to quick load a previously quick-saved game.

A prompt will appear to confirm the quick-load.

Press YES.

The game will be loaded automatically.

Can I change the keys?

Of course! Go to Options -> Controls and you'll see the key bindings there near the bottom right.

Do check out the controls section to see what keys you can rebind.

Conclusion

This feature was made based on feedback and requests by customers like you. We've always listened and we hope you'll like what's being done so far.

Thanks for your support as always.

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Patch V1.07c-1 released!
notes.content:
Dear all,

Due to the urgency of some of the issues reported, we've decided to release part 1 of V1.07c patch as V1.07c-1.

The build ID is - 684182.

New Implementations
- Burn effect now is more pronounced; you'll definitely know when a ship is being burned.

Modifications
- UNC repair costs, rates and delays have all been corrected to reflect the actual value. Not all ships and structures will have the same percentage of worth of repair vs building a new unit. Every unit will have its own unique factor and value.

Simply put - it's fairer and more worthwhile to repair ships and structures now.

Good: Fair price, doesn't cost an arm or leg to repair ships anymore, making repairs worthwhile.

Bad: Repair delays has been adjusted - some structures used to be in "god" mode as long as they're being repaired and multiple ships can't even take it down. This is no longer possible. Ships and structures in general will now take longer to repair to its full health.

Fixes
- FIXED the black triangle issue PERMANENTLY. Tested with high particle density with a special test set that emits lots of particles unnaturally - no black triangles observed.
- Fixed a rare but serious bug where the game suddenly disallows you from picking a ship or drag-dropping to select ANY ships.
- Fixed a bug where customized flight paths can be created across sectors that have wormholes that are ALREADY sealed.
- Fixed a bug where failure to create a flight plan with a fleet doesn't cause a notification to appear in the main panel and/or fleet panel. In fact, the fleet panel incorrectly reports that fleet is heading towards that sector.
- Fixed a bug where enemy ships under construction inside an enemy shipyard can actually fire their weapons. This is no longer possible.
- Added message to inform player during multiplayer if a game can't be created due to a lack of a network device. Previously, the "Create Game" button doesn't do anything if there isn't a network device.
- Fixed a problem between fleet selection and 2-step orders such as attack, move and launch bombers. Buttons used to appear incorrectly or even randomly, exposing incorrect functionality - this has since been fixed.
- Fixed a bug where loading games doesn't read the amount of time previously given, causing the next game to always report the full amount of time played even when the previous block had already been reported. (thus making it easier to get the play hours achievements).

Conclusion

That's it for now. The next batch will contain Pugalenthi's new voice and other minor bug fixes.

We're sorry that some of our new customers might have encountered the regression errors introduced during implementation of certain new features and that might have led to a lesser impression of Foresight.

Please try Foresight again and do not hesitate to let us know if there's a problem.

Thanks,
Jeremy

notes.title: V1.07b Patch Released!
notes.content:
Dear all,

We've finally released V1.07b patch. This is a bug-fixing patch more than an implementation patch. Nevertheless, there're some important implementations as well.

Implementations

1) Implemented mouse sensitivity to deal with mouse with differing DPIs used on different resolutions. Because DirectInput takes raw data, the final input is not adjusted against Window's own mouse sensitivity. To that end, we've implemented 2 things:

a) An automated tuning system that scales based on a default height ie, 768. Therefore, if you're running 1080p, the mouse is automatically 1.4x more sensitive.

b) If the automated tuning system isn't enough or is making your mouse go at roller coaster speeds, there's a user-defined mouse sensitivity introduced - IN Options -> Gameplay -> Mouse Sensitivity. This is an adjustable bar which will immediately take effect when changed. (without the need to click apply, but you'll still need it to save the value). Adjust till you're comfortable - ie, a single move from left to right should get your cursor across the screen without the need to lift your mouse.

2) Added safeguards around steam calls so that in an event of an exception the game might not crash that easily. We'll try to handle it as much as possible - this is a blind catch, steam might still cause the game to crash beyond our means to understand why.

3) Added automated port forwarding for folks who want to try out the multiplayer. However, the IP address is still required for your friends to join. This will be done away with in the future. (Yes I promise, a steam-integratd lobby WILL be up). The server setup is now handled by a thread, which eliminates that nasty hang while waiting for the server to be up (about 10 seconds for some cases).

4) Automated LOD system implemented to automatically cut certain unnecessary emitters off, thereby improving performance and almost certainly eliminate the black triangle, poly syndrome problem with ATI users.  How does it work?

a) Based on your Graphics -> Particle Density settings, the game will apply a limit on certain unnecessary particle emitters that will stop emitting when the total number of particles has reached a certain level OR the frame rate has dropped below a certain number.

b) If your frame rate drops below, ie, 30 fps - which is the mark for Medium settings, some emitters will stop emitting temporarily until the performance improves. High setting will have higher tolerance towards frame rate drops.

c) If the total amount of particles is too high, it'll cut. All game-affecting particles, ie, bullets, lasers etc will take priority. Therefore, if there're more ships firing at each other, even if your system can take the load, the game will limit itself before it hits the maximum particle threshold (before the black triangle aka poly syndrome appears). This is not a 100% fix as there might be a scenario where more than 10,000 bullets/projectiles can appear on screen at once, that will certainly cause the triangle effect on ATI cards.

d) The experience will be a little stuttering for slower machines. But we'll continue to take in feedback and make the necessary adjustments if need be.

Changes

1) For Mission 2, objectives have been modified to state more clearly what you're supposed to do. You're supposed to find the pirate and arrest him.

2) For Mission 5, it's discovered that the models all look pretty black and oily due to the angle of lighting. We've adjusted the lights to have a little more ambient so that you can see your ships and the enemy ships better.

3) IFF colours now look more obvious and you'll definitely know if that ship is yours or not better. Though, this has come at a cost; the IFF bands no longer react to diffuse lighting, and thus might look a little awkward under certain angles. But we recognize that players will value identification more over asthetics when they play. Again, we'll make modifications as necessary if there's feedback.

4) The following 2-step orders will no longer remove from selection when executed.
a. Move + position or ship
b. Attack + ship or position (attack move)
c. Launching Bombers + ship
This is to allow players to change their minds if they need to last minute on their targets and/or positions.

5) For Mission 5, neutral UNC ships will no longer attack you just because you accidentally fired upon them from behind. This hold true until you purposely target them. Upon knowing that, those neutral ships will turn hostile against you... permanently. Otherwise, stray hits will no longer cause that to happen.


Bug Fixes

- Listbox issues, scrolling, showing the final item, etc are all fixed.
- Fixed a bug where combined selection of ships, with the buttons clashing against each other at their designated position, some commands like request for NSAU gauntlet can still be triggered EVEN when the button isn't visible.
- Fixed a bug where sub-widgets that are hidden can actually trigger a onMouseOver event causing the cursor to change state.
- Fixed a small bug where selection ring colours are not updated when joining or leaving a fleet.
- Fixed a small bug where choosing fleet 1,2,3,4,5 to join fleet doesn't have any ESC button. The only way is to deselect and re-select the ships.
- Fixed a bug with timing achievements where everybody can get a 250 hours playtime achievement even when they've just played for 2 minutes. Achievements attained will still persist despite the fix.
- Fixed a bug where fleet requests may NOT always be on top. This is because not all fleet requests have asked to be insert from the top.
- Fixed a bug where NSAU turrets can sometimes exit from a wormhole looking weird like a glowing pancake.
- Fixed a bug where NSAU turrets can sometimes move up or down so much that they're effectively useless.
- Fixed a bug where NSAU turrets can sometimes IGNORE your will to move them even when their destination line is based on yours - they'll just drift away. That's fixed.
- Fixed a bug where NSAU turrets sometimes have a hard time going through wormholes. They take longer and almost certainly must be in the throat before going through.
- Added feature to allow fleets to be selected by CTRL+ double-clicking them.
- Added caching to introduction so that the cutscene will flow more smoothly while it transitions between scenes. (in some cases, the music even stopped for a short moment). Note: The real fix for this is to thread load the assets so that any delays will be borne by the thread, not the main game itself.
- Improved display resolution robustness for frequency rate failure. This will ensure that Foresight will always pick a supported resolution at the lowest refresh frequency FIRST if the default resolution isn't supported.
- Fixed a bug in Options menu where some options were never reverted correctly when Revert / Default button is pressed. (and confirmed)
- Fixed a bug where UNC ships are not deselected when they're chosen to be repaired by the Global Repair tool. It causes confused when the player double-right-click to cancel the tool, causing the ship (still selected) to move away thinking that it's a move order.
- Fixed a bug where fighter blips weren't displayed due to an incorrect condition. By default, fighter blips are displayed to highlight whose fighter/bomber belongs to who by holding TAB (default). Green means they belong to you. Red means the enemy. Yellow means allies and Cyan - neutrals.
- Fixed a fighter return approach issue where in certain cases, the fighters can overshoot the hangar causing it to drift out of the map until it stops - then it'll auto-recover and tries to land in the hangar again. This behavior is incorrect and is potentially deadly to exposed fighters/bombers. Now it's fixed to retry the moment the hangar is BEHIND its final approach vector.

Some fix requires a mission restart to apply. Ie, materials and lighting.

notes.title: V1.07a splash damage INDICATOR changes
notes.content:
Dear all,

I forgot to mention one very important change that you may or may not have noticed. Splash Damage indication.

Due to the mix of distortion and other effects, chances are you won't even know you've been hit by your enemies or you've dealt splash damage to your enemies and inadvertently yourself as well.

As a result, we've changed the indicator to RED color to indicate that a splash had indeed taken place.

Promethane Gas Volatility

We've mentioned many times that the gas is volatile - meaning that if you HIT something inside the gas cloud, the cloud will violently explode, inflicting additional damage on your target(s) and possibly your own bombers as well. 

This means EVEN if your weapons do not cause splash damage, the cloud will splash it for you.

A splash damage inflicted within a gas cloud is magnified on top of the gas' own splash damage.

Complex Splash Mechanisms

There're some weapons that can do splash damage and at the same time, inflict status effects on your ship due to the proximity of the splash. For example ... SS Bio Turret ejects a Proximity Bacteria bomb which upon detonation, will splash and spread the bacteria onto targets within the same area.

Conclusion

Not many ships are armed with weapons that can inflict splash damage. But those who do should be used with caution. Have fun!!

Regards,
Jeremy

EDIT: P.S. The splash damage mechanism itself wasn't changed. Sorry for the misleading headline.

notes.title: V1.07a patch released!
notes.content:
Dear all,

V1.07a patch has been released to address certain issues and implementations.

Implementations

1) Implemented support for monitors with refresh frequencies other than 60hz.
The following frequencies will be supported:
60Hz, 70Hz, 75Hz, 80Hz, 85Hz, 90Hz, 100Hz, 110Hz and 120Hz.

2) Implemented change to the resolution list to include bpp and refresh rate along with the resolution. So instead of seeing just 1920x1080 for example, now you'll see 1920x1080x24 60Hz. Therefore you might see 1920x1080 more than once.

3) Implemented fallback system when a new resolution is changed. This is to address input not support issue when the player accidentally switches to a resolution that is supported by the graphics adapter but NOT the monitor. A countdown of 10 seconds will start - the player must click YES to accept the changes or the game will revert to the previous resolution automatically.

Fixes

- Fixed a small bug in Mission 30 where the briefing text doesn't correlate with the voice over.
- Fixed the weird seams that appear when the game runs in Windowed mode. This was due to Windows borders and panel taking up some parts of the width and height.
- Improved the particle density option by applying a setting to ALL emitters that will be emitting in the game. Improved overall performance.

Conclusion

More improvements to come you way. Thanks for your support as always!

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Reminder - Fighter and Bomber behavior specifics
notes.content:
Dear all,

Again, this is an reiteration on some of the fine details of fighter and bomber behavior.

There's a bonus sight radius system in Foresight that bestows 10% of additional sight radius PER fighter registered in the hangar capped at 100%. This means a ship with 10 or more fighters or bombers will have 2x sight radius.

Let's talk about bombers first:
Bombers

1) They do not conduct patrol and will not engage enemy fighters
2) Their primary role is to attack a given target
3) Targets can be changed by re-launching them at the new target (the bombers will turn and attack the new target)
4) Bombers will not intentionally fly through enemy obstruction; instead, it'll either fly above or under the obstruction. Thus, surrounding important structures with other structures DO make sense.
5) Bombers with payloads (ie, torpedoes, bombs, etc) will continue to attack even after they've exhausted their payload - with their primary weapons.
6) Bombers will automatically return to their mothership EVEN if she might not be in the same sector. That means you can launch bombers, get out of the sector and wait for them to return.
7) The angle of launch is important. Launching them in the enemy's face means that theyll face a lot more counter fire before they can attack.
8) Bombers under your command will only return when their primary target has been destroyed OR by your command to do so. (Recall bombers)
9) It is possible to force your bombers to attack enemy fighters ... though highly not recommended unless it's a desparate move.

Fighters

1) Fighters automatically patrol around their mothership and will attack any nearby enemy fighters or enemy bombers that attacks their mothership.
2) FIghters can also attack enemy ships and structures as a supporting force. This act is limited by default to a certain distance away from the mothership. Once this distance is breached, the fighter will automatically return to the mothership. (Pursue and Destroy standing orders ignore this rule).
3) Fighters too might have ammunition such as intercepting mini-bombs.
4) Only 5 fighters will ever attack a single enemy fighter. This is to prevent a weird behavior and an incorrect lure conclusion - where a single enemy fighter can drag the entire flight of fighters to attack it. This rule doesn't apply to enemy ships and structures.
5) You don't need to keep your fighters to cross wormholes; patrolling fighters will automatically follow their motherships into the wormhole.
6) Pressing STOP on your mothership will cause her fighters to go into a reset mode. The fighters will by default return to the mothership to conduct space combat patrol. However, if there's an enemy fighter nearby, it may pick it up and continue its attack.

Tips and Tricks

1) Fighters and Bombers can be launched concurrently.
2) It's better to have 2x carriers with 6 fighters each than 1x carrier with 12 fighters. 2 carriers deploy fighters 2x as fast and will achieve operation readiness earlier.
3) Have a good balance between fighters and bombers. Interceptors are considered specialized anti-fighter crafts. They're technically considered as fighter-class but they're not advanced fighter-class.
4) Time your bomber launches well, coupled with proper in-battle intelligence from scouts.
5) Do not launch bombers headlong into enemy capital ships. They'll suffer heavy casualties. Instead, move to a good launch position and deploy them so that they can attack the enemy from the flanks or rear instead.
6) Do not try to play catch-up with enemy ships running away from you; they'll not outrun you but they can lure you into dangerous positions. Instead, use bombers or fighters to pursue.
7) Bombers are more well-armoured than you think.

Conclusion

That's about it for fighters and bombers. More intricate details of Foresight will be released soon! Stay tuned!

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Reminder - What happens to the fighters when your capital ship is destroyed?
notes.content:
Dear all,

I find it important for us to reiterate certain not-so-obvious behavior within Foresight to keep everybody well-informed.

We all know that fighters and bombers form the backbone of all massive operations - being the tide turner. However, all fighters and bombers require a mothership to reside at. Without a mothership, the small crafts will very soon run out of fuel and self-destruct.

Extra Hangar Space
Therefore, it's important to bring along extra hangar space. An empty carrier, frigate or even a destroyer can be used to recover orphanated fighters and bombers.

Recovery
As long as they're in the same sector, orphanated fighters will automatically find the nearest available mothership to return to. 
(obviously, they'll be able to rejoin the fight soon after)

Last Fight
When fighters and/or bombers are attacking a target and its mothership is destroyed, they'll still continue to attack the enemy ship until they themselves are destroyed OR that enemy ship is destroyed. During this time, they will NOT self-destruct - making them extremely sticky to deal with.

Additional hints on fighters/bombers
1) UNC fighters/bombers can be repaired up to 75% of their hp only. Nothing more.
2) UNC ships all have different repair rates, UNC Carrier being the highest.
3) Think of repair rates like engineer crew team size. A larger crew can focus on repairing on repairing a single fighter faster. Having more fighters forces the crew to be divided.
4) SS fighters/bombers won't regenerate when deployed.
5) SS fighters/bombers regenerate in the hangar regardless of blood pool levels.
6) NSAU fighters/bombers shields recharge as per normal BUT can't be repaired even in hangar.
7) NSAU fighters/bombers shields recharge twice as fast while in the hangar.
8) Bombers actually can RUN OUT of ammunition. Recall them to replenish their warheads. (doesn't apply to NSAU Bomber).

Have fun!!

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Foresight V1.07 Release Notes
notes.content:
Dear all,

Here's the release notes for V1.07

 New Features 

- Foresight now officially have Steam Achievements. Some require progress, some require grinding and some require certain skills. Have fun!

- Added an achievement gallery in the Options menu where you can see the progress of your achievements and some statistics. P.S. I don't like how the statistics are presented as well and will some day in the future improve the look and feel of it.

- Added a cutscene gallery in the options menu (only accessible from main menu's options) to allow you to revisit Thomas Lock's journey throughout the entire campaign. Cutscenes can be unlocked retrospectively. That means, if you complete the LAST mission in the campaign, you'll unlock ALL the cutscenes.

- Certain mission achievements are awarded retrospectively as well.

- UNC Repair mode can now be used on ships as well. However, there must be a UNC Shipyard in the current sector for it to work. It will not send ships back to remote locations automatically.

- Implemented Quick Save and Quick Load. Default keys are either Ctrl+F5, Ctrl+F7 OR F6 and F7 depending on whether if it's a new install or existing. I'd advise you to change your keys for your own comfort. Quick save requires 1 save to be done so that it can remember which slot to save at. Quick load depends on that as well. That way you no longer need to go into the options to save.

- Added new resolution support.
1) 1600x1050 (16:10)
2) 1440x900 (16:10)
3) 1280x800 (16:10)
4) 2560x1440 (16:9)
5) 2048x1152 (16:9)
Reasoned that even though the 2D sprites might stretch, the 3D assets won't be stretched that much. The scene should still look nice despite the higher than recommended resolution support.

- WINDOWED mode is up!
Yes! For those who are very used to doing Alt+tabs in/out and having problems restoring Foresight under Steam client - now you can use Windowed mode. It's located in the Options -> Graphics - Select Windowed checkbox and press Apply.

There're some changes to this.
1) Alt+Enter no longer switches between modes. This switch was never recommended and it doesn't correct the aspect ratio properly most of the time, leading to weird looking squashed or stretched graphic glitches.
2) Foresight will try its best to fit your desktop resolution. This may or may not be possible. If it's not possible, you might end up with a larger than usual window - which you can fix by selecting the right resolution in the list.
3) We're well-aware that despite having windowed mode, there's a slight inaccuracy in the vertical pixels, causing certain blending lines to appear at certain Y heights. This is due to pixels being allocated to Windows border and top frame. We'll resolve this in due time.

P.S. Alt+tab issue disappears completely with windowed mode at the expense of roughly 8-15% of performance. V-sync isn't allowed in Windowed mode and will be automatically disabled if Windowed mode is chosen.

Enhancements

- Improved the way fighters, interceptors and bombers die across all 3 factions. The key is to randomize a wait instead of having a fixed waiting time. This will allow some breathing space for processing and improves the overall randomness of fighters' death sequence (especially when they're all killed at the same time)
- Slightly optimized fighter deaths by reducing the number of particles they emit during the sequence.

Bug Fixes

- Fixed a bug where level 0 shortcut key binds can be modified, but isn't reflected in-game until the game is restarted.
- Fixed a bug in the Controls section where SOME of the key bindings are actually not shown. Now, the whole set of possible key binds will be shown.
- Fixed a bug when a game is loaded, UNC Command Centers or NSAU Strongholds will allow you to build another structure EVEN when it's supposed to be building its current structure. This causes the existing u/c structure to remain in semi-transparent state and it simply goes into limbo without recourse.
- Fixed a bug where a ships being selected aren't updated correctly when the PLAYER (ie, Thomas Lock) jumps into another sector. Ship in command radius are supposed to lose all options immediately. This fix mostly fixed the graphic side of things - the gameplay isn't affected.
- Fixed missing featured voice actors in the prologue cutscene.
- Fixed a problem with multiplayer chats for clients who might see double or more PER message sent.
- Fixed a bug for client-side NSAU turrets where the turret appears not to be charging itself.

P.S. I might edit this announcement if I missed out any information.

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Steam Cloud enabled
notes.content:
Dear all,

I apologize that we took SO long to get this up and running. We should have done so in the first place though there were other issues and considerations that were discouraging us from doing so.

Steam Cloud pickups

In any case, Steam Cloud for Foresight is up. Basically, the following things are automatically saved into the cloud:

1) Campaign progress
2) Saved games
3) Key bindings

Please note that - if you have installed Foresight on multiple machines with different saved games - only the latest copy will be uploaded onto the steam cloud.

Therefore, please either:
1) Save again into an empty slot
2) Rename the saved game manually via browsing local game files -> /saves/ForesightSaveN.fss (where N stands for the slot number)

Pros

1) Obviously, even after uninstallation, your saved games will be preserved and be restored when you decide to re-install Foresight again.

2) This also works if your HDD has crashed or for some reasons, some processes wiped out the saved game.

3) Lastly, it's good if you need to play Foresight on another PC with the SAME steam account.

Cons

1) Only the latest saved game will be taken - so if you have HAD 2 saved games occupying the same slot - chances are it'll be overwritten by latest copy.

2) Total number of save slots reduced to just 1 set - if you had multiple copies installed across different machines - the saved games occupy their own slot and will never be overwritten.

Conclusion

After much consideration and taking into account player behavior - it's best that we adopt the steam cloud solution so that you'll be able to access your saved game anywhere anytime and always have a backup in case your local copy is corrupted or missing.

P.S. You'll still need to delete the corrupted file manually - best before exiting Foresight.

notes.title: Announcing an improvement in UNC repair tool (global repair button)
notes.content:
Dear all,

Observing several gameplay/review videos, we've discovered that while the global repair button seems to be intuitive for repairing structures, the notion that UNC ships have to be repaired at a UNC Shipyard seems a little not so intuitive.

After consultation with a few Foresight players, we're going to implement the automation for this button.

Pick and Choose Design

1) Click on the "Global Repair" button
2) Ensure that there's at least one local shipyard available and you have sufficient power.
3) Click on the damaged ship

That's it. The ship will automatically proceed to the nearest shipyard for repairs.

Dual-Option Design

We could also implement the following -
1) If you select a bunch of ships and press the "Global Repair" button, it'll do the same thing for multiple ships like above.
2) If you click the button first, then individual ships being selected will actually cross sectors (if necessary) for repairs. This move is risky even when the safe route is taken.

Conclusion

Please tell us how you feel and how we can make Foresight easier and more intuitive for you to play.

Thanks,
Jeremy

notes.title: V1.06n released!
notes.content:
Dear all,

Patch V1.06n has been released. Sorry for taking so long. This patch is meant to address bugs and issues encountered recently. As mantis is already back up again, we'll be logging issues more proactively as we encounter them or when there's a feedback.

Build ID: 620031

Fixes

Scenarios:

1) You recruit Commander A and assign him to a ship. Then you create a fleet, then he goes out, fights a battle and dies. Now you receive a message, saying that Commander A is at sector ABC and is available for hire. So, you go back to your command center and look for him. He's there - except that you can't click on the "Recruit" button. Instead, you can move him.

So, naturally, you'll try and the game crashes.

Fix Implemented:
1a) Fixed regression bug that doesn't regard the officer as dead
1b) Fixed messages pertaining to losing commanders you can't hire. P.S. If you're a Captain, you can't hire a Commodore. So you shouldn't be receiving a message telling you Pugalenthi is available for hire when you can't even see him at the sector the game reported.

2) In a multiplayer game - you create a fleet with a commander but realised that you wanted SOMEONE else to be the commander. So, you try to shift the commander out to another ship to disband the fleet. The game crashes.

Fix implemented:
2a) This only affects the SERVER player in a multiplayer game regardless of whether if there's any real human clients joining the game. The reason is simple - when a fleet is disbanded, the object is straightaway invalidated - somehow this was misunderstood when the server tried to send the packet. Data management issues.

3) Fleet View doesn't appear if Fleet is in transition.

As mentioned before, we wanted the fleet view to always appear regardless of transition. This is now in the game. However, there's only 1 problem we've yet to resolve - that is the automatic multi-ship selection updates should the fleet be going through a wormhole in the same sector as you are. Should be resolved by V1.07.

4) A bunch of stability loopholes had been fixed. They might have led to bugs that might have crashed the game in a manner not known to us. Fixing it should improve the stability of the game at the very least.

What's next

Barring any major issues that might pop up, we'll continue to work on V1.07 features - which is quite a few. We'll also look into things like "Full-screen windowed mode" and other options that was raised as a feedback previously.

We'll continue to fix any issues encountered - clearing the mantis bug list; V1.07 will be released latest within 2 weeks (end May).

Thanks again for your support. We're really excited to release V1.07 soon so that everyone can enjoy the new features we'll be bringing into the game!

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Announcing V1.06n patch
notes.content:
Dear all,

Understandably, there might be some of you that might have encountered a specific problem when commanders under you die. Though you can do a workaround by reloading the game, right now, you can't re-recruit commanders that was defeated and allowed back in-game a while later.

There were also several bugs discovered along the way, with multiplayer as well.

Originally I'd have preferred to wait till the art assets are in and we can deploy V1.07 as a full major patch. But we now know the artwork's not going to make it in time.

Therefore, we'll have to work out an interrim patch to address the problems that were made known to us some time back. Those problems were already fixed but unable to deploy immediately due to the concurrent work with V1.07 implementations.

We therefore apologize for this inconvenience and assure you that work is still very much in progress - our pace hasn't reduced.

One of the key obstacles is to "disable" steam integration which we've already done in order to get your achievements uploaded. This though, a simple step but also a tricky one as well - which takes time to ensure that nothing is broken when we do that.

I know we've been working on V1.07 for quite some time already and I can confidently tell you that we're on the verge of finishing it already. All that remains is the artwork and the combined testing that is required before we do any patch releases.

Please bear with us for the next 1-2 weeks. We'll release an interim patch to address the issues at hand and will fix the rest by V1.07.

Thanks,
Jeremy

notes.title: Patch V1.06m released
notes.content:
Dear all, V1.06m patch has been released. Build ID: 601915

This patch is a major bug fix patch which will have a significant impact.

Implementations

1) Groundwork for achievement is basically up. But the UI and steam integration isn't done yet along with the artwork integration. There'll be a stats file generated; there's no need to care about that file for now. Stats collection may be possible; ie, your progress in terms of cutscene unlocks, mission level achievements, destruction/loss ratio, kills, losses etc will be recorded.

2) New music for Prologue Cutscene with opening credits!

No more elevator music. A proper music has been arranged for this cutscene to fit the occasion. Added some opening credits as well to keep the scene less boring.

Fixes

- Fixed mission 1 repetitive lines where Nathan Nunis keeps repeating "we're not done yet, whelp!" That's not supposed to happen. He should only say it just once.
- Adjusted mission 1 quota back to 5000 instead of 4000. Don't worry, this is done for balancing, the UNC harvester now harvests much faster to keep up with the SS and NSAU harvest speeds.
- Adjusted mission 1 reinforcements to come sooner. Be careful of those bombers.
- Fixed mission 3 Frigate reward should your actions be too fast for the script. Previously, if you are too good, the script skips rewarding you that extra frigate. Now it's definitely rewarded as long as you fulfill the tutorial requirements. No REWARDS for skipping the tutorial. ;p
- Fixed in various mission the direct use of Ship-NNNN identification. Now Foresight will use 6-digit ID instead of 4. This is done so that the game can withstand at least 99999 crafts at any one time.
- Fixed in various missions where officers of the same faction but in enemy camp were ALLOWED TO ROAM ABOUT. This allows you as the player to recruit them ONLY for the AI to hijack them from you onto their waves. This causes a glitch in the fleet panel and crashes the game should you try to move the fleet. The fleet panel will also show an invalid picture of someone who's supposed to be there but isn't. 

Now characters who are in the same faction but in different enemy camps will no longer even appear in the recruitable list. Codes were modified to allow the AI to pluck them out of obscurity and put them as a commander.

- Fixed a MAJOR bug in the renderer where unused vertex buffers aren't reallocated to other needs. This causes an out of range scenario where the game will typically crash almost certainly after a chain of 16-20 missions. This includes restarting missions as well.
- Fixed officer descriptions where errors were found.
- Added instrumentation for achievements for all the missions involved. Those they do trigger an achievement, the final system isn't up yet to register it with Steam. (You won't have the achievement stored locally either yet).

EDIT: You may have to restart your mission if it starts to behave strangely. Though we do not foresee such a case happening - but if it does so anyway, please restart your mission. If it's a single battle, it's probably better to start a new game. (this is due to the ship ID format being changed from Ship-XXXX to Ship-XXXXXX - this may cause script misfiring to occur) 

As you can see, we're pretty near the end point towards steam integration. I'll be looking forward to integrating with the Steam API in a couple of weeks. More exciting things to come!

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Patch V1.06j released!
notes.content:
Dear all,

Thanks again to community feedback, we were able to uncover more intricate bugs more easily and apply a proper solution to it. We've also included some things that were marked as V1.07 release to be released early for your playing pleasure.

Implementations
- Added GFX card info used to run Foresight. This is useful to help players do some troubleshooting on whether if they're using the right GFX card to run Foresight or not. This applies heavily to folks with dual-graphic cards on laptop.
(To see, press Alt+F when you reach the main menu)

- We noticed that Earth's clouds were of sub-standard quality even at 2x1k texture. Therefore we've replaced them with much higher quality clouds for your viewing pleasure.

- Whenever NSAU runners return to the sector where their NSAU Stronghold lies, they'll do another local search to see if there's a nearby stronghold to unload their valuable cargo. This is implemented to reduce time to ship credits to you as well as to avoid potential ambushes.

- Implemented a simple colour scheme for command point usage. We recognize that users may be confused by the apparent 0/24 usage. Is that half-empty or half-full? That means, a user may mistakenly thought that 0/24 means having NO MORE command points remaining (when it's the opposite).

Now a colour scheme will tell the user that when it approaches RED, it's time to build more fleets or kill more enemies to get promoted.

Fixes
- Sometimes the NSAU Mobile Refinery may just stop there doing nothing. Pressing 'A' (default) doesn't get it to move. Users have to manually click a few times to urge the mobile refinery to harvest from a particular gas cloud. This has since been fixed. Harvesters will henceforth be more proactive in resolving their situations.

- Fixed a misleading tip where a NSAU Micro Laser Turret or NSAU Heavy Laser Turret isn't powered, a tip appears to get you to start their shield overdrive. This is not possible and has no effect since they have no energy.

- Fixed a bug where fighters left behind may end up chasing targets from another sector inadvertently in the local sector. (Blind chase effect).

- Fixed a bug where fighters seemed to be interrupted while jumping across wormholes. At the end of it, they might just hang there without moving at all.

- Fixed a multiplayer CLIENT bug where a Sirerian player will hear opposite EVA messages when triggering Blood Burst. (ie, Blood Burst On - EVA says Blood Burst off)

- Fixed a bug where a user-based launching of NSAU Mobile Refinery RUNNERS were blocked by a validation code. Upon validation, the whole code is skipped, causing the whole command to fail. Runners are always deployable regardless of harvest/refijned volume in the Mobile Refinery.

- Fixed a bug with NSAU Runners where under certain circumstances, they'll NOT move to their Strongholds and do nothing about it. Increased proactivity and will to resolve difficult situations.

- Fixed a bug where a NSAU Runner being attacked will ACTUALLY conduct a fighter attack run on its attacker. This behavior is wrong and totally unnecessary.

- Fixed a major bug for single-player morph structure order. This applies to ALL who convert themselves into structures. Ie, SS Salvager, UNC Harvester and NSAU Garrison Ship. The code didn't add 1 to the index after using and since the new structure by morphing doesnt' appear until the craft reaches the spot, it doesn't use the index - causing others like structure placement orders to use it. This causes an index conflict where only 1 vessel will respond to the player when clicked and may not even be at the same spot due to index hijacking.

- Fixed a bug in Mission 25 where Maximilian Cornelius isn't hidden from the mission.

That's all for now folks! I'm still working on a strange bug in Mission 26. We'll try our best to resolve it properly and release yet another patch soon.

Thanks again for your support!
Jeremy-

notes.title: V1.06i patch has been released
notes.content:
Dear all,

As I've mentioned earlier, V1.06h patch was aimed at fixing several acute issues that were reported while we were optimizing the multiplayer. As such, there were several items that were left out or weren't properly done. One of which is the wormhole exit mechanism.

We worked as quickly as possible to deliver V1.06i patch - which consists of several important fixes.

Therefore I present V1.06i patch - Build ID: 577585. Please update your copy of Foresight.

Fixes

1) Fixed / Finished implementation of wormhole optimization exit code. The original code works on single player but have problems with multiplayer in terms of correctness and synchronization.

2) Fixed a bug where the default BBLibCfg.dat file was tainted during deployment. As a result, the game will try to start in 1920x1080 even when it may not be supported. A proper file has since replaced your current copy for this patch. This is for the folks who might have encountered Foresight failing to run the 1st time.

P.S. By updating to this patch and running Foresight, the "unable to create render device" should go away. If not, please post on the discussions page. I'll be more than happy to assist you.

3) Fixed a potential bug where players might be able to assign orders to ships that switched factions. Fortunately, this only occurs in Campaign mode.

4) Fixed a bug where evacuation of officers can be done even when the ship that was previously selectable, now isn't due to some script events. By allowing officers to move away like that, it may cause a problem since officers can't move into ships that are unselectable. As a result, this patch fixes the rule. If the ship is no longer selectable, the officers onboard will not be considered for evacuation. Though, this only happens in Campaign mode.

5) Revamped Mission 24 after extensive feedback on play style and game possibilities. Now, the mission has been redesigned to be stricter with what it really wants and updates the objectives more often. Enemy patrols will no longer be impeded due to timing and will always attack as planned. (Can't reveal much due to spoilers).

Note: Ship capacities do NOT matter when the script assigns new characters onboard. This is a new rule so as to faciliate story telling without being impeded by gameplay possibilites. P.S. Lock will still be required to bring either the Avenger or Endeavour to the objective. This will be enforced in-game as well.

Conclusion

After this patch, barring any further issues, we'll head back into multiplayer optimization and correction of behavior. After that, we'll head into stats and achievements, integration with steam API and eventually, the full multiplayer match making system.

Thanks for your support and understanding! Your feedback makes Foresight a better game! So please, keep them coming!

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: V1.06h Patch Released!
notes.content:
Dear all,

Due to a report on a bug - ie, cutscenes turns into a white screen, we've quickly investigated and found the problem and of course, fixed it.

Build ID: 576160

The reason for the delay in this patch release is because there were some revamps going on with the transition system (across sectors). On top of that, as of now, V1.06h multiplayer will not be compatible with any older versions of Foresight, but will be compatible with the upcoming V1.07 patch.

Fixes
- Fixed the white screen cutscene issue. Tested on Nvidia GeForece 840M, Nvidia GeForce GTX 550 Ti, ATI Radeon HD 7770.
- This patch contains optimized multiplayer. That means, if you try multiplayer now, it'll run a lot faster even in heavy combat situations. Though I've not tried it across the globe yet.

Known/Existing Issues
- The transition appearance is slightly off at the moment due to some direction calculation errors but doesn't affect the stability of the gameplay. This will be fixed in due time, or by V1.07
- Mission 24's issues remain - I'm sorry that I couldn't get it fixed in time. Please be assured that this will be the next issue on our list.

Conclusion

We are very grateful for your feedback and thus was able to know that such a problem exists. We apologize if you were unable to see the introduction or prologue cutscenes. In order to see the intro, please go to 

Options > Gameplay

and check on "Always play introduction cutscene"

To view intro, please restart Foresight. After which, you can go back to the options to disable it.

Yes, one of the features on the list will be a cutscene list where you can reminisce on your past adventures.

Thanks again for your support! We look forward to hear from you. Please feel free to make a post on any issues; we'll be there to reply you asap.

Regards,
Jeremy

Regards,

notes.title: Announcing major patch V1.07
notes.content:
Dear folks,

We've commenced working on V1.07 - which is a major patch that will take at least 3 weeks to complete. By the end of it, we should have the following:

1) A more lethal AI based on a revamped code design and shifting of responsibilities between script and code.

2) A more stable and optimized multiplayer.

3) Trading cards (should be available BEFORE V1.07 is released)

4) Integration with Steam API - foot in door level. I can't guarantee if match making will be available by then, but it's definitely in the right direction.

5) Revamps for mission 1, 2 and 3. Tutorials will be removed and placed as separate playable missions.

6) Revamps for adding certain space objects into the game. If all goes well, these objects can represent new environmental hazards and killing zones (other than Promethane gas *wink*)

That should be all for now. I hope that more can be achieved by then. But meanwhile, please enjoy playing Foresight!

P.S. NSAU's mobile turrets have been redesigned. However, old saved games will cause those turrets to be permanently disabled. My suggestion is to restart the mission just once. V1.07 will fix migratory problems such as these.

Have a great week ahead!

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Foresight V1.06f has been released
notes.content:
Dear all,

After quite a long break, I'm proud to announce that V1.06f patch has been released.

EDIT: Build ID : 555414

This patch deals with quite a fair amount of issues - some were based on regression errors that were introduced in V1.06e.

Here're the new implementations:

1) NSAU Micro Laser Turret and NSAU Heavy Laser Turret will now gain the ability to MOVE while not being powered. But in exchange, it can't fire (obviously) and its shields will be down. But that shield will be restored to its original amount when charged again. The mechanic is similar to going dormant.

2) Adjustments made to the bloom effect to reduce conflicting graphic information AND over-exposure of explosions that descends into white patches instead of showing the explosion texture. Bloom still exists but at a more subtle level.

Doesn't apply to NSAU Stream Laser Turret!

Default behavior still applies to NSAU Space Dock.

Fixes:
- Fixed a scenegraph issue that causes the game to be slower than usual
- Fixed Mission 24 where conditions to win the game is more focused and clearer.
- Fixed a bug where allied fighters and/or bombers will be launched as a counter-attack against allied ships that attacked itself using direct-hit weapons such as UNC Vulcan Cannons. This is no longer possible.
- Fixed a bug where a NSAU structure powers down and keeps playing the low power sound.
- Fixed a bug where due to a stricter enforcement on ship types, it causes Foresight Introduction ships and some cutscene ships to be skipped during creation. This doesn't crash the game but does cause the game to look a little weird.
- Retaliation code is now optimized on single and multiplayer.
- Fixed a bug where subtitles no longer appear on screen - the translucent letterbox still does but no words will appear.
- Fixed a bug where selecting an enemy ship and then opening the strategic map will cause its flight plans to be revealed.
- Adjusted various widget position and size for both 16:9 and 4:3 resolution UI
- Fixed a bug where a selected item in the list of items doesn't completely cover the entire item. Ie, a request in the fleet panel.

notes.title: Foresight V1.06f has been released
notes.content:
Dear all,

After quite a long break, I'm proud to announce that V1.06f patch has been released.

EDIT: Build ID : 555414

This patch deals with quite a fair amount of issues - some were based on regression errors that were introduced in V1.06e.

Here're the new implementations:

1) NSAU Micro Laser Turret and NSAU Heavy Laser Turret will now gain the ability to MOVE while not being powered. But in exchange, it can't fire (obviously) and its shields will be down. notes.title: V1.06e patch released!
notes.content:
Dear all,

V1.06e patch has been released for update. This patch is a little different since there were optimizations made to the game - though incomplete, they'll still make a slight difference in your game's performance.

Build ID: 534648 (please make sure your build ID at this ID before running Foresight)

Implementations
- Optimized collision handling, reducing the amount of searches and string generation required. For heavy battles, it could make a difference.

* Note: This doesn't apply to multiplayer yet. The whole optimization process for multiplayer is expected to take longer ~2 weeks to complete with testing.

- Optimized retaliation code, reducing the amount of proxy calls it does and therefore optimizing multiplayer. Retaliation code works everytime a ship is hit - thus more efforts will be put into optimizing this method.

Fixes
- Fixed a weird behavior in the retaliation code where a ship will hestiate at who to fire back. This is the wrong behavior. Once an enemy ship is picked for a counter-attack, it'll stay on attacking the enemy ship till its destroyed before moving on to the next.

- Fixed a bug that is caused by clicking on buttons that will disappear after, causing the ray caster to be disabled. This creates the impression that the UI is blocking the game's picking functionality where in reality it's actually be disabled and in certain cases, not being re-enabled.

The workaround is to click on another button that doesn't disappear; like the global map button. The only way to select a ship during then is to drag and select.

- Fixed a bug that causes a crash when a player regards another player as an enemy. This is a campaign-only feature since skirmish modes do not have neutral modes and alliance cannot be broken.
Affected missions include:
1) Mission 6
2) Mission 10
3) Mission 20
4) Mission 21
5) Mission 22

(EDIT: Forgot to add this)
- Fixed a faction naming spelling error with NSAU Government. In the previous version, the word "Government" was mispelt as "Goverment". Embarassing I know. Fixed in this patch.

(EDIT 2: Forgot to add this as well)
- Did a small code review and discovered that the fleet commander sometimes make a very dangerous assumption that the wormhole does lead to somewhere. Fixed it to check before using the destination sector.


GDC 2015

Finally, I'm proud to announce that Foresight will be joining our Singapore group of delegates heading to San Francisco for GDC 2015 under the booth known as Singapore Gamebox.

During this period I'll personally be there and work on Foresight will be suspended temporarily till the 12th of March. Even so, I'll be on the watch for any issues that pop up and will try to provide a workaround.

Thanks again for your support! We're looking forward to complete whatever we've envisioned to do for Foresight after GDC!

Namely:
a) An easy to access and match-make multiplayer (not to mention stable)
b) A more solid AI that can kick your ass really badly
c) Steam trading cards (which should be available by 12th March, we're already working on it, making badges that look nice enough for your liking)
d) Steam stats and achievements - currently 100 achievements have been planned out. More to come. I envision at least 120 achievements in total will be put into the game.
e) NEW GAME MODES!!! Yes - the survival modes we've discussed will be implemented.

notes.title: V1.06d - Quickfix patch is released
notes.content:
Dear all, the latest patch for Foresight been released.

BuildID: 528953

Please verify your game's integrity to make sure that it's properly updated.

Fixes
