notes.title: V1.06c quickfix patch released.
notes.content:
Dear all,

A quiet bug hidden in the tumblers have been found thanks to community feedback. One can imagine it to be in one of the the doors of that endless tunnel.

Yes, this bug has been around for a long time but due to its unique way of triggering - it has eluded my grasp.

Fixes

- For UNC only - if a structure is under repairs, the hint to prompt u to get it repaired will not appear. More improvements will come.
- Small fix: When a game is loaded, it loads all the logs as well. However, if u share ur saved game with another player who might hav a different resolution, the font size will be different. Now it's fixed to always follow the local font size.
- Fixed a small bug in mission 1 where a script will keep running even when it's no longer required to do so.
- Adjusted mission 22 to start victory evaluation earlier.
- Fixed a major bug mentioned above:

The bug only appears with the following sequence:
Save > Load > Save > Load (this load uses incorrect data)

1) All scripts have a progress indicator of where they're now. This progress is saved properly during the 1st save.

2) However, during the first load - the progress is read, adjusted into the script but lost because it's not read into the object. At this point, the game is still playable and will not exhibit any script-related bugs yet.

3) During a 2nd save, incorrect data is now being saved, ie, both positive and negative progress being 0.

4) During the 2nd load, the game is now bugged at this point. Scripts may appear to be restarted without reason even when the conditions to fulfil it was met long ago. Exactly like what had happened in mission 22.

Additional notes

It has come to my attention that some of our players have tried to do a 5+1 fleet attack on a single sector. For ATI card users, there's a grand limit particles that can be taken in with the current design even with batching and buckets.

Once that limit is breached, black triangles will start to appear and might even cause a crash due to data being read and erased at the same time.

We'll probably have to bring forward plans for a "dynamic LOD" system which will automatically cut down particles emitted during heavy duty periods. More to be announced in the future.

Conclusion

It's not a good feeling to find a bug that has beeng causing players problems. However, I try to be as transparent as possible - to show that I'm really working on the issues and doing my best.

Therefore, please help us by providing community feedback so that we can make Foresight a better game for you. :)

Thanks,
Foresight Team

notes.title: V1.06 is out!
notes.content:
Dear all, first of all sorry for such a long delay. I was down with a viral infection that had effectively halved my productivity. Secondly, there were some urgent bugs found that had to be fixed and I had to conduct extra tests to ensure that nothing else is broken after the fix.

BuildID : 522155

In any case, this is a reasonably huge patch and will have quite a few things packed in it.

Foresight OST

As a token of appreciation towards those who had supported Foresight when she was first launched, we've included 2 original soundtracks of Foresight in 256kbps mp3 under your main game folder \OST.

1) Cloudy Cosmic.mp3
2) Suspicion.mp3

These 2 tracks are available for free. More tracks may be included in future patches BUT they will be removed at a certain point in time. Therefore, if you like our OST, please save them elsewhere to continue to enjoy them.

Cloud Cosmic - Written originally for mission 10, depicting its situation
Suspicion - Written originally for mission 15, also depicting its situation.

For those who've played these missions, you might notice that they're always the 1st song on the list to be played whenever the mission starts at the beginning.

Implementations
1) Implemented Fleet View that represents the view of a fleet when you select your fleets. It has several important features in it, ie, 
a) (prompt) Evacuate!
b) Auto-assignment of Fleet Advisors (a free officer must be onboard one of your ships in the fleet)
c) ETA timer for estimated time to arrive at destination that you've set. It could also be a patrol craft you've crafted. The timing is based on the slowest ship in the fleet.
d) Viewing of ships in its situation, ie, alike multi-selection view, except that you can't choose individual ship types due to the possibility that they may be at different sectors at one time.

2) Multiple construction/spawning system. You could now select multiple builders and assign individual build/morph orders to them. The game will automatically seek the nearest builder and assigns it to an order and deselecting it from the selection.

(As shown in the V1.06 preview video)

3) Now structures of the same type in general can be grouped.
4) Deployment positions can be assigned to multiple shipyards
5) Multiple shipyards can be selected at once and a single click builds N-number of vessels. Ie, if I select 4 shipyards and click on "Build UNC Frigate" button - 4 frigates will be built AT ONCE.

6) Informed the need for port forwarding to be done for multiplayer games. Ie, now players will know which port Foresight is using for multiplayer.
7) Implemented a fair system in which when a ship's stats are being changed, the player will retain the stats by percentage. Ie, if a frigate's stats was 500/1000 - now if i reduce that max hp to 800, the player will get 400/800 stats. Likewise if I increase the max hp to 1200, the player will get 600/1200.
8) Added auto-correct for range in option menu to avoid out of range crashes.

Balancing

The following balancing has been done to Foresight. SS players will hate me for it but will thank me when playing against another SS player in the future.

1) NSAU Punisher - reduced 5 hull points to 60
2) NSAU Gaunlet - reduced 10 hull points to 45
3) SS Seeker - reduced 300 hp, from 750 to 450.
4) SS Salvager now requires 2 more seconds to spawn
5) NSAU Explorer reduced 100 shields points to 350
6) Normalized ALL command point usage:

 All harvesters and runner class vessels now take ZERO command points
 All anti-fighter class vessels take 2 command points
 All Frigates-class (excluding NSAU Lens Cruiser) takes 3 command points
 All Carriers-class vessels take 5 command points
 All Siege-class vessels take 6 command points
 All Destroyer-class vessels take 9 command points

7) Corrected the size of UNC Democracy hangar. Should have been 6 instead of 16.
8) All special ships in the game will no longer take up command points. I can't mention here due to potential spoilers.
9) SS Bastion and SS Citadel will both take additional 4 seconds to spawn

notes.content:

BuildID : 522155

In any case, this is a reasonably huge patch and will have quite a few things packed in it.

Foresight OST

1) Cloudy Cosmic.mp3
2) Suspicion.mp3

These 2 tracks are available for free. More tracks may be included in future patches BUT they will be removed at a certain point in time. Therefore, if you like our OST, please save them elsewhere to continue to enjoy them.

Cloud Cosmic - Written originally for mission 10, depicting its situation
Suspicion - Written originally for mission 15, also depicting its situation.

For those who've played these missions, you might notice that they're always the 1st song on the list to be played whenever the mission starts at the beginning.

Implementations
1) Implemented Fleet View that represents the view of a fleet when you select your fleets. It has several important features in it, ie, 
a) (prompt) Evacuate!
b) Auto-assignment of Fleet Advisors (a free officer must be onboard one of your ships in the fleet)
c) ETA timer for estimated time to arrive at destination that you've set. It could also be a patrol craft you've crafted. The timing is based on the slowest ship in the fleet.
d) Viewing of ships in its situation, ie, alike multi-selection view, except that you can't choose individual ship types due to the possibility that they may be at different sectors at one time.

notes.title: Why can't my ships follow each other?
notes.content:
Alright, actually this feature was already implemented right from start. However, it was overriden by some regression errors and a follow order ended up as an attack order.

This will be fixed by V1.06, which is - by this Saturday.

There're basically 2 types of follow:
1) Follow in the sector only, doesn't follow ship out of the sector lest it gets ambushed on the other side

2) Follow all the way, but you'll need to hold CTRL to trigger it.

But remember, if your ships can fire upon the enemy ship, it WILL do so unless the standing order - Silent Tail is set upon the ship designated to follow.

Silent Tail

If set to silent tail standing orders, your ship will always follow the targeted ship even if it's an enemy ship and will automatically follow it across sectors. As such you don't need to hold CTRL to trigger it.

notes.title: V1.05c patch released!
notes.content:
Dear all,

V1.05c patch has been released officially. Here're the list of fixes and improvements we've done so far:

Implementations
1) Added mission and campaign description in the mission objectives under options. So you'll know all these information (options > mission objectives) without the need to save a game.
2) Scoreboard events can now be accelerated by holding the LEFT mouse button. (RIGHT mouse button for left-handers). Everything in the scoreboard will speed up up to 3-4 times.

Fixes
- Added device incapable tests in post processing effects (at least for distortion effect now) to disable the effect should the device be incapable of performing the efect.
- Fixed a bug where texture quality and anti-aliasing options are disabled AFTER a game. (you go back to main menu, options and you can't change them)
- Slavic Sirerian Obliterator doesn't update its texture properly when it heals above 50% hp.
- Small planet sample is bugged. Fixed it to eliminate orientation and that weird line issue.
- Fighter tag icon can be triggered as long as you're in-game. That is no longer possible until the main bottom panel is up. (ie, it's pretty weird to see a fighter tag icon appearing over the shuttle in mission 1).
- The sudden increase of volume in the main menu when you continue campaign is now fixed.
- Fixed a flaw with Mission 17 where the mission can go into a limbo state; ie, you can't win or lose the mission under certain circumstances. Now those triggers have been fixed.

Conclusion
- This is a small patch that fixed a few important bugs albeit small bugs, could affect your gameplay experience. V1.06 is currently in implementation and should be released by Friday, if not Saturday pending test results.

notes.title: PLANNED: New single/multiplayer game mode - Survival
notes.content:
Dear all,

A new game mode has been planned for and will be one of the 2 additional game modes to be added into the game, free for all existing customers once it's tested and deployed.

Survival

You and your friends have been surrounded. Enemies come from all directions and will wipe you out the moment anyone slips up.

Survival is a co-op multiplayer or single player (co-op with bots still under consideration) game mode that is along side the standard skirmish battle mode.

Survival games will have different maps that will be designed to suit the needs of the game mode.

Difficulty

There'll still be the 3 difficulty modes - Easy, Normal and Hard AIs. Based on the factions assigned to each AI, ships and fleets will be spawned to attack your base after an initial timer runs out.

Thus you'll have a reasonable amount of time to build up your defenses. Harvesting is still enabled for additional funds.

Economy

On top of harvesting and initial credits, you can also earn credits by destroying enemy vessels. For every capital ship destroyed, you'll earn 1/3 of its total HP. Ie, a UNC Medium Frigate yields 333 credits. A fighter is worth 100 credits apiece and a bomber, 250 credits apiece.

Co-op

In a co-op game, with a maximum of 4 players, all 4 players will be spawned in the SAME sector, in the middle, each with their own base structure in a diamond formation.

The game feel will be similar to campaign mission 13, except that the waves will be increasingly harder to deal with.

Time Limit

For the standard survival mode - there'll be a fixed time limit for each mode. Right now, the numbers are 10 minutes for easy, 25 minutes for normal, 45 minutes for hard. They're NOT the final numbers.

SIEGE BREAKER mode

A planned deviation from Survival. This is not an additional game mode, but rather a small mod from the main mode.

In this mode, every enemy spawning point will have a command center. Upon its destruction, you'll stop an AI from spawning further ships and existing ships that belongs to that particular AI will cease to function.

- The destruction of each command center yields 25,000 credits to all players.
- Waves will NEVER end, no time limit
- You win when you destroy all the enemy command centers while withstanding endless waves of ships.

Please discuss your thoughts in the discussion topic named - "Survival and Siege Breaker"

notes.title: Announcing V1.05c patch
notes.content:
Dear all,

A small patch will be released latest by tomorrow that addresses several minor bug fixes and a potential mission stopper bug. One of the things that is fixed is the ability for the distortion ability to consider a device incapable possibility due to various reasons. Once it's determined that the device is not capable to handle distortion, it'll become inactive. Incapability can be caused by a wide variety of reasons; not necessarily due to shader support.

On top of that, there'll be 2 new little features added:
1) You can now make the scoreboard run faster ~3x simply by holding down your LEFT mouse button.
2) Mission objectives in the option menu has been updated to show the campaign and mission description - so you don't have to save a game just to know which mission you're on.

V1.06 will still be on for next week's weekly build.

Thanks!

notes.title: V1.05b has been RELEASED!
notes.content:
Dear all,

V1.05b has been released as build 510716. This patch mainly focuses on fixing very hard to find bugs as well as any regression errors reported earlier. It's a continuation from V1.05a - with some features added.

=== New Implementations ===
- Volume calculations has been corrected. You may have to adjust your volume for music. The lowest volume will still be 5% loud. If you must, please switch off the sound component completely.
- All in-game sounds will be dampened by 65% whenever there's an in-game speech going. This is to enable you to listen to what the speech is about without in-game sounds interfering. However, you may want to zoom the camera upwards if the sounds are still too loud for you.
- Implemented sound bank module for future use.

=== Adjustments ===
- Adjusted scoreboard's title text per item in 4:3 resolutions to be slightly away from the item progress bars.
- Small planets are corrected in their texture orientation. Previously it was mirrored horizontally.
- Reduced the amount of time needed for intelligence information to EXPIRE. This means if you've spotted a structure, it'll not last that long even after your scout has left the area. The purpose of this adjustment is 2 fold. 
1) With perceived enemy presence, the OST Juke Box will always play battle music even when you're not in the danger of fighting.
2) Now you'll need scouts in the area (dormant or not) to constantly update the intelligence on the field. Otherwise that intelligence will expire and be removed from your player intelligence database.
- Adjusted harvester-class ships and structures to be avoiding other friendlies completely as long as they're found to be in the space. This only applies to harvester-class ships/structure; other ships have an increased arc compared to previous patches. This means, all ships now are less tolerant of other ships in its vicinity.

=== Bug fixes ===
- Fixed a bug where a previously dead commander, after being resurrected and assigned to a new fleet, will cause the old fleet panel to be visible.
- Fixed a bug where reassignment of fleets in the same slot cause the fleet text to be printed incorrectly in the fleet panel.
- Fixed a bug where a ship is assigned to a fleet and the selection ring colour doesn't change (and vice-versa).
- Fixed a bug where the mission briefing room will continue to brief the player when a dialog box appears as the game ALT+TABs in and out. When the game is restores, the mission briefing continues even when the dialog box is still waiting for an answer.
- Fixed a bug where ships that are not affected by the command radius limit DO NOT HAVE ANY COMMANDS after they're being assigned to a fleet. This also means that you can't unassign them unless the fleet itself is in command radius.
- Fixed a bug where structure builders within the fleet doesn't leave the fleet properly when the player task it to build/morph into a structure.
- Fixed a bug where enemy presence isn't taken into considerations when plotting a safe path. Now enemy presence serve as a more serious deterrent compared to uncharted sectors.
- Fixed a bug where fleet panels inadvertently even when invisible, blocks out mouse clicks, causing ships to suddenly be irresponsive even though it lights up when you hover your cursor over it.
- Fixed a major bug with saving games where the AI can suddenly go lame without further action. That should explain why some players are able to defeat HARD AI without any losses while suffering some loss dealing with NORMAL AI.
- Fixed a bug where Fleet Advisors cannot be demoted.
- Fixed a bug where replaced Fleet Advisors continue to be appointed as a fleet advisor by status.

=== Conclusion ===
There're still several less severe bugs out there to be fixed gradually. But the good news is I'll be able to focus more on implementing more features that will help improve your experience in the upcoming V1.06 patch!!

Have a nice weekend!

notes.content:
Dear all,

Finally, V1.05a patch has been released! This patch primarily fixes bugs that were found along the way. Some were discovered very much later because it takes a very specific combination of conditions to trigger it.

Anyway, here's the list of bug fixes:

1) Fixed a bug where sometimes harvesters-class ships, ie,  UNC Harvester, SS Salvager and NSAU Mobile Refinery doesn't automatically move to the next resource patch when they've exhausted their current patch.

2) Fixed a bug where certain ships, usually scouts, when given a flight plan, will end up circling around their final destination. This is not a default behavior.

3) Allowed "Personnel" button to be present when ships go out of command radius. This is so that officers onboard can be given the orders to create a new fleet; you no longer need to recall that ship back to create a fleet or assign an advisor.

4) Fixed a usability bug where a single click on ships that belong to a fleet which is outside of your command radius to automatically select the ENTIRE fleet. This disallows Scouts, Harvesters to perform their intended duties AND normal ships to be UNABLE to leave the fleet if desired. However, this functionality is still retained. If you press CTRL and click on the unit, it'll select the entire fleet.

5) NSAU Mobile Refinery doesn't show its progress in construction when clicked upon. Ie, you build a mobile refinery with your NSAU Stronghold and click on the mobile refinery under construction. Now you can see its build progress.

6) Fixed a bug that incorrectly warns the player when moving certain ships across sectors. Vessels that are not subjected to command radius limitation will NOT trigger a warning anymore.

7) Fixed a small bug where the game doesn't inform the player that there're no more resource patches in the sector when "Harvest" button is clicked.

8) Fixed mission briefing text spills for 4:3 resolutions for Mission 14. (Thanks to Doomdancer for the find).

9) Fixed mission briefing clearance timing in Mission 16 where the assets clearance can be skipped.

10) Fixed a bug where the player is advised to assign a ship to fleet EVEN when that ship already belongs to a fleet.

11) Rolled back applying bump maps and specular maps onto UNC Command Center, UNC Outpost, UNC Refinery and UNC Shipyard. These were originally experimental to see if there'll be a significant improvement in graphic details. Unfortunately, for some reasons, it's overriding the material alpha which causes it to be opaque at all times regardless of conditions - it breaks the game when a structure is supposed to be obscured but yet somehow can be seen.

A decision was made to roll back these changes for the following reasons:
a) Having bump maps and specular maps does add a bit of improvement, but not significantly enough.
b) Removing it also reduces the amount of VRAM being used by these maps.

12) Ensured that no unnecessary textures or normal/bump maps were loaded  when it's not used. This will free up a few MB of VRAM which could be essential for those running on 512MB VRAM.

13) Foresight has been rebuilt with Large Address Aware enabled. I've read certain articles that it may not be a good thing on 32-bit systems with 4GB of RAM. However, we'll standby and monitor for your feedback. If the game becomes unusually unstable in this patch (which I've tested at least for 60 minutes without issue), then we'll consider reverting to non-LAA enabled.

14) Fixed a weird bug that causes Foresight NOT to generate ANY logs. This is due to a weird condition that skips the creation of the log file completely.

15) Fixed a bug where incorrect texture combinations were assigned onto certain ships when they take too much damage.

16) Fixed a bug where custom flight plan for ships without a fleet always pushes the ship to CENTER of the map by default. Custom paths will always end at the final sector after exiting the wormhole regardless of the ship having a fleet or not.

17) Fixed a bug where an attempt to switch the ship chase cam to a fighter chase cam fails due to validation and the player is unable to press ESC to return to tactical view.

18) Adjusted accumulator description for mission 27. (Accumulators are statistics you see on your default view when no ships are being selected)

19) Added notification to the player when a fleet is being selected under special circumstances, ie, Ctrl+clicking a ship that is out of your command radius. It serves to quickly inform you which fleet has been selected.

20) Fixed a rather embarassing bug where you can assign flight plans to ships that DON'T BELONG TO YOU. Now that's no longer possible.

21) Fixed a bug where double-right clicking on the sector hexagon can switch sectors. This behavior is wrong. Only double-left clicking can trigger a sector change.

22) Fixed a bug where normal ships doesn't move using a safer path by default. All flight plans by default moves with safety in mind first. If you want to barge through a series of sectors or get the shortest route there - hold CTRL when you right-click select a sector. (Naturally it doesn't apply to custom paths since it's CUSTOM)

23) Fixed a major bug with NSAU Mobile Refinery where Runners can be lost - the runner was considered deployed and not in the hangar but a series of conditions complicate the deployment and causes the Runner to be in a limbo. Since runners cannot be recalled, they're not inserted into the sector, they'll be stuck in a limbo totally, taking up precious command points. Now the deployment mechanism has been revamped to accommodate the various complex scenarios the mobile refinery might face during deployment.

=======================
That's about it.

There WILL be a V1.05b because there're still some outstanding bugs not fixed yet. But no worries, those are not game breaking bugs.

Thanks for your patience and support!

P.S. Developer really needs to take a break now.

notes.title: V1.05 Released!
notes.content:
Dear all,

V1.05 has been released. This patch improves some of the fundamental gameplay mechanics which will really make certain things much easier than before. However, as it involves the core codes, a lot of testing was required to ensure that regression errors do not surface as a result (ie, fixing one, breaking another).

Highlights

Supply Routes
* Supply routes NOW matters. Previously, your fighter deployment, ship deployment to fleet, harvester return paths from remote locations will all head straight even when there're unexplored sectors in-between. While it's definitely faster, it runs a high risk of encountering enemy base fortifications which will wipe out your units before you even notice.

Have a safe secure route allows the AI to plot a safer path back to base automatically albeit slower. Naturally, to improve the supply route, you could always explore and secure more direct routes to improve shipment times.

Customized Flight Plan for ALL

* You can now assign a flight plan to ANY units that can be moved. The process is the same as fleets. Select 1 or more ships, open the strategic map, right-click OR hold CTRL to plot your path.

All non-fleet ships will have paths designated as WHITE. If you select multiple ships with multiple paths, the strategic map will render all those paths as well ; possibly messy but gives a direct overview on units headings.

Tips and Tricks

Tired of looking at the same loading screen? Well, now you'll have tips printed everytime the loading screen appears. They're random and will cycle if loading takes longer than usual.

Don't ignore these tips; they can be extremely useful in your campaign or future battles.

Sirerian Mobile Blood Pool

* SS Mobile Blood Blood Pool comes in during certain missions roughly between Mission 15 - Mission 20. These half-structure half-ships previously take on the properties of a normal structure; therefore has many rules not available to them. 

Now this is resolved; they no longer will hinder your gameplay by forcing you to move them ship by ship, to sector by sector. They now can be multi-selected, grouped, and be given a flight plan at your whim.

 Bug Fixes and new Implementations 

* Fixed a bug where loading games under certain conditions will crash especially when the Strategy Map button is being pinged.
* Fixed a bug in Mission 4 where there's a line where Jun Jimin talks without a voice.
* Fixed a small bug with the Rank progress indicator where it seems to outcrops a little in 16:9 resolution.
* Option Menu now goes in levels - Press ESC will go back by 1 level until the main Game Journal menu before heading back to the game with a final ESC.
* A small deployment flag is now shown if you set a deployment position with a shipyard.
* Reduced the glare of the explosion glows so that it doesn't overexpose the explosion and wipe out the texture behind. This is to improve the look and feel of the game.
* Improved the texture used for clouds on Earth.
* Fixed a bug where scouts or other ships sometimes rotate needlessly around its final destination.
* Fixed a camera bug in Mission 11. This is caused by fighter-chase cam interferring with the script cam.
* Increased the amount of time you'll have to reach Vasily in Mission 11.
* Fixed a small bug with the options type text where it may not be updated properly, ie, graphic options but showing "Controls" instead.
* Fixed a bug in the multiplayer client where the blood burst mode is never shown even when it's initiated by the player.

Final Notes

Safety-paths may not always be the way to go since it depends highly on how you explore the sectors in the map.

Basically, safety-path creation will always try to avoid unexplored sectors if possible but might end up taking an extremely long route.

In any case if it fails or IF the destination is too close for any safety planning to be of use, the given path will be a direct one.

And also in any case should a safety path fails to be created due to unforeseen circumstances, ie, complex map paths, paths that are way too long for the ship to traverse, the AI will generate a direct path instead.

 What's next? 

I'd expect trading cards to be ready anytime next week. But that will not interfere with V1.06's plans - which is to improve the user interface, graphics and some other aspects including the AI.

 Conclusion 

Once again, thank you for your support and feedback. We look forward to hearing more from you soon!

notes.title: V1.04 is OUT!
notes.content:
Dear all,

We've glad to announce a major patch to Foresight - V1.04. (BuildID 487410)

First of all, I'll like to apologize to the folks who have been limited by the fixed shortcuts of Foresight previously. This is especially so for European folks using different types of keyboards. But, in V1.04, you'll be able to assign your own shortcuts based on your own keyboard's layout to almost all Foresight commands.

The new controls interface isn't a quick fix and wasn't intended to be in the game initially. It was through feedback from users like you that we discovered and recognized this problem. Thus, we hope you'll be able to get a better gaming experience after updating to V1.04.


 Controls 

There're many controls available and some controls are "layered". This means, although they're in the same category, they only appear at different times, thus allowing the same shortcut key to be assigned to it.

These layers are differentiated by teal, green and red. As long as the colours are different, you're allowed to assign the same key as a shortcut.

An example would be - getting a ship to join a fleet >
Fleet -> Join Fleet -> Assign to Fleet 1
or
Officer's Quarters -> Officer's Mess -> (Pick a commander)

Notice there're 3 layers in this instance. In each layer, the same buttons do not appear together at the same time, thus allowing them to share the same shortcut keys if desired.

The key binding system is as flexible as it can be, barring certain keys from being used, ie, F12, Alt+tab etc... but it's possible to have long key combinations like Ctrl+Shift+Alt+Numpad 5 ... while it's technically possible, we highly discourage that since such a combination makes a shortcut... not so short anymore.

Multiplayer

We fixed a host of issues pertaining to multiplayer and some regression bugs as well.

1) Now there'll be more synchronization points for ships
2) Fighters no longer appear out of nowhere (unless syncing)
3) All clients and server will not stop execution even when you deactivate the game application. The game will still run its logic without rendering in the background. Of course, this only applies to multiplayer and you must already be in a game session prior.

 List of issues fixed 
1) Fixed texture for NSAU 16:9 panel
2) Fixed texture for UI list box so that it won't look so translucent.
3) Changed the texture for plasma burns to a more fire-realistic variant.
4) Fixed a small problem when you head into the campaign mode and suddenly there's a loud boom of sounds of fighting.
5) C2End cutscene assets are now cached prior so eliminate any jerking. No difference to memory usage; flow is improved.
6) Fixed a bug with Salvagers having a -65XXX% harvested during multiplayer games.
7) Fixed a bug where EVA doesn't report a unit construction complete for fighters and runners.
8) Implemented auto-reflection for tool tips that will reflect YOUR desginated shortcuts, not the default ones.
9) Fixed a bug in mission 20 where Ganymede is missing.
10) Fixed a bug in mission 8 where the player's assign path of escort isn't properly related.
11) Fixed a bug in the mission briefing room SAVE feature - requring you to press BACK to return to the game. That's no longer necessary and any options changed will not cause a prompt to appear.

**  There were a lot more implementations and bug fixes that can't be listed out here.

We hope that with this fix, everybody will be able to at the very least, see where all the commands are and remap it if necessary.

With this, we'll head back to looking at some of our gameplay improvements for the next patch, which will commence development next week.

Thanks again for your support!

notes.title: Progress on V1.04
notes.content:
Dear all,

This is an update to let everyone know that Foresight V1.04 is still very much in progress. The system that allows key binding requires a separation of action from key assignments. This takes a whee bit more time than expected since there're quite a few considerations - RTS have a lot more actions that can be bind to keys.

However, unlike other games, some keys CAN be repeated due to commands be made in 2 or more steps. Some keys can't be remapped though.

In any case, every (almost all) action will have their assigned key shown.

If all goes well, this patch should be out earliest on Sunday, latest by next Tuesday.

Multiplayer

A lot of changes have been made to the multiplayer to make it more playable and stable. One of the biggest changed made is to allow the game to run in the background even when it's deactivated, so as not to mess up the synchronization. (Rendering is skipped of course)

More tests will be conducted to ensure that your multiplayer experience is as smooth and bug-free as possible.

That's all for now folks! Heading back to work.

Regards,
Jeremy

notes.title: Running Foresight on Laptops with 2 graphic cards
notes.content:
Introduction

It has long known to us that some laptop models may have 2 video cards built into it known as Integrated and Discrete video cards respectively.

In some cases, Foresight is started using the Integrated card and might:
1) Failed to run with a message - "Failed to start render device"
2) Managed to start running but has a lot rendering artifacts, blinking particles, etc etc.
3) Or, managed to start running as per normal but is extremely slow.

Please make sure that Foresight is being selected to run on your Discrete video card instead. This can be found usually in the video card's driver application, ie, AMD Catalyst.

Power saving mode

It's also known to us that sometimes laptops will switch between Discrete and Integrated based on power settings. Ie, with AC power or without AC power.

Such a switch during runtime will cause Foresight to crash.

Therefore, it's recommended to either maintain using the Discrete video card or temporarily disable power settings.

Conclusion

Please feel free to post a discussion topic should you face any problems starting Foresight. We'll be more than happy to assist you.

notes.title: Guides Update
notes.content:
Dear all,

Thanks again for all your feedback and suggestions. If there's anything you want to know in detail, you could try to hover your cursor over the button for half a sec and the tool tip will appear. If it doesn't, they could be disabled in the options. (Under Options -> Gameplay -> Tooltips)

Of course, if you're still confused, please do not hesitate to post a discussion. We'll get back to you as soon as possible - and if possible, post a Guide soon after.

A lot of details can be found on www.foresightrts.com - but we understand it's disruptive to alt+tab in/out of the game. Therefore, the guides on Steam itself should be accesible via Shift+TAB without much disruption to the game.

We're doing our best to make things easier and fun for you to play Foresight. Therefore, please go ahead and post a discussion so that we can help you as soon as possible.

Thanks again!

notes.title: V1.02 is out!
notes.content:
Dear all,

Foresight V1.02 has been released. Please update your copy of Foresight if it's not set to automated update. The buildID is 472293.

Fixes:
=====
- Tooltip description fixed for certain ships
- Fixed a clash of shortcuts for certain ships
- Waypoint arrow pointing issue fixed (triangle sometimes point at the opposite direction)
- Black triangle glitch fixed.
- Fixed a fleet panel reporting bug where the commander repeatedly reports attacking local target even when the target is at a remote location.
- Provided a workaround for "Input not supported" issue. This issue stems from the fact that your monitor may not be able to support resolutions your video card does. We're only able to detect the resolutions of whatever your video card supports. Therefore, instead of picking the best, we'll pick your desktop resolution instead as it's confirmed to be a working resolution.

If the resolution is too low for your liking, feel free to change them in the options. However, it's best to know if that resolution is supported by your monitor or not first. One way is to test it with Windows first before doing so in Foresight.
- Fixed a bug where you can select a ship while looking at an officer's dossier.
- Fixed a few other minor bugs.

Implementations
=============
1) Shipyards, Citadels and Bastions now can have rally points called "Deployment positions" in Foresight.

Select your structure, right-click anywhere to set the point.
Note that if you set the rally point, the default behavior of the ship is now overriden by the rally point movement. (ie, harvesters won't automatically go harvest if you set a rally point on the shipyard it's being built from).

To reset a rally point to default, click on that structure and right-click itself. You'll see a message that the deployment position has been reset.

2) V-sync is now an option under Options > Graphics - check or uncheck to set the option and click on Apply to apply it.

3) Added gameplay option - introduction is no longer being played everytime the game starts (default). You could check it to play the intro everytime it starts. The only exception is the 1st run - the very first time you run Foresight, it'll always play the introduction.

4) Added gameplay option - Double-clicking approves fleet requests. (Default is off). If you think it's faster to double-click to approve a fleet request, just check it and apply.

However, do take note - when you double-click, another identical request can appear straightaway.

5) Multi-selection can now be manipulated in 2 ways.
i) Select a ship type and only that type will remain in the selection
ii) Hold SHIFT and select to deselect a particular ship type from selection.

6) Improved double-clicking selection -
Hold CTRL + double-clicking selects ships of the same type with or without fleet depending on the first ship selected. Ie, if there're 6 gunships, 3 belongs to a fleet, 3 is free, you can select all the free gunships by holding CTRL and double-clicking on one of the free gunships.

You could do likewise to ships in a fleet. Same example, hold CTRL and double-click on one of the gunships in a fleet, it'll select all gunships from the SAME fleet only. Makes it easy to reassign to another fleet or leave the current fleet.

7) Holding ALT key will reveal shortcuts of ALL the possible functions you're seeing on screen. However, we're still not too pleased with how it appears on the buttons - since no matter what colour we used, it'll clash with the icon behind. Therefore, we'll work to see how we can better improve the shortcut display.

8) Caching is now enabled for pre-loading certain assets to reduce "jerking" while doing so. This applies mostly to cutscenes only.

9) Added more hints and tips to give you advise based on certain situations, ie, out of command points, ships' health are getting too low, what can you do with it? Etc etc. In future revisions, these tips will be optional (checked under gameplay options) and will cover more areas.

10) Implemented hangar status updates for ships with hangar. Will post a guide to show you in detail what each status mean.

11) Now every unit/gas/wormhole can be centered upon by clicking on its portrait after being selected.

12) Implemented a fighter/bomber IFF system where you'll be able to track the location of your own fighters and bombers by pressing TAB. This is currently a key-hold toggle. Once you release TAB, the IFF information will be hidden. A quick overview:
Green = Your own fighters
Green bomblet = your own bombers
Light green = Your fleet's fighters
Light green bomblet = your fleet's bombers
Yellow = Allied fighters
Light Blue = Neutral fighters
Red = Enemy fighters
Red Bomblet with a tinge of yellow = Enemy bombers

Will improve this system to include your own commander movements. Might reveal enemy commanders IF scouts are in the area to see them.


=== V1.03 preview ===
- Possible key mapping feature for some features of the game.
- Possible additional of buttons to zoom right into attack reports. Ie, harvester under attack, ship under attack, fleet under attack, etc.
- Possible auto-LOD system that limits non-gameplay particles from being emitted. This will be the comprehensive solution to resolve the black triangle glitch problem for ATI/AMD card players.
- Campaign mode will have an additional prompt
1) Tutorial mode (Starts from mission 1)
2) Expert mode (Starts from mission 4 onwards, rank is given with reasonable amount of XP for progression)
- Possible option to allow middle mouse button to act as the knob scroll trigger. Set as an option under gameplay options.
- Possible tips system - a random tip display while the game is loading.The tips can be reviewed under options separately.
- Possible specialized view for Fleets, with 2 portraits - 1 for the commander, 1 for the advisor, along with other important fleet information. Shows up whenever you select a fleet.

notes.title: Folks, V1.01 is out!
notes.content:
Dear all,

V1.01 has been released. As promised, we've listened and are still listening. Please make sure that you make a backup of the "save" folder under

Foresight > Properties > Local Files (tab) > Browse Local Files... (explorer opens) > "save" folder. This is only a precautionary measure in any case thing happens while updating.

V1.01's build is based on BuildID: 462462. If it's not this ID, it means the game isn't updated yet.

Fixes:
- Escape key now works to open and close the in-game options menu.
- Vsync is now no longer forced. While it's switched on by default, you could do this:

Foresight > Properties > Set Launch Options...
In it type: -novsync

- Font size adjusted for tool tip description
- Some buttons that have long descriptions now auto size the captions.
- Fixed a bug in default view when loading a game saved in a previous resolution, the items are wrongly position.
- Fixed a bug where the destruction of structures yield no points.
- Reduced unnecessary waiting times in-between missions.
- Harvester in Mission 1 will not die unless you're in the same sector as it and still do nothing to help it. It'll still take some damage, but will have a reasonable amount of hit points when Thomas Lock arrives to help.
- Enemy Frigate in Mission 1 is now destructible.
- Quota in mission 1 changed from 5000 to 4000
- Reinforcements in mission 1 now come faster
- Removed unnecessary camera locks in mission 1 during the tutorial. (especially after the combat tutorial)
- Removed unnecessary camera locks in mission 2; the ships are still locked until the player fulfils the basic steps of building a base.
- Fixed a weird problem where the waypoint/guide arrow goes missing. They're back on now.

Implementations:
- Added a load-filler screen in between long loading times. Applies to everything except single battles where loading time is almost non-existent.
- Objectives are now always shown for a short period of time whenever the game starts or is loaded from a saved game, or when there's an update to the objectives
- When a unit strays out of command radius and is selected, the player will be prompted to act upon it.
- Message is now printed to tell the player if they've attained the maximum XP allocated for the mission.

Known issues:
- Sometimes the waypoint/guide arrow points in the wrong direction. We're exploring different ways to fix this problem as soon as we can. 
- Input not supported issue - as mentioned, we'll find a more elegant solution and will incorporate it into our next update. Most likely, it'll be a command you can pass as arguments into the game and there's no longer a need to switch to windowed mode.
